disclaimer.title: Educational use only
disclaimer.body: VetClinPathGPT is a study aid. It does not provide diagnoses, treatment recommendations, or professional medical advice, and it must not be used to make decisions about a patient. Generative models can produce confident errors — verify everything against primary references and a qualified clinical pathologist.

sections.title: What it is
sections.body: A free, openly available AI tutor for veterinary clinical pathology. It works conversationally: a learner brings a question, a set of laboratory values, or a case scenario, and the tutor walks through the reasoning rather than simply returning an answer.

sections.title: Who it is for
list: DVM students working through clinical pathology coursework
Veterinary interns consolidating laboratory interpretation on the floor
Practising veterinarians refreshing clinical pathology fundamentals

sections.title: How it should be used
sections.body: As an educational aid that supplements teaching, textbooks and specialist supervision — never as a diagnostic system. It is most useful for rehearsing interpretive reasoning: why an acid-base pattern fits a differential, how to build a systematic approach to a haemogram, or where a cytologic description leaves ambiguity. Learners are expected to check its output, and disagreement with the tutor is itself a productive teaching moment.

sections.title: Educational research
sections.body: The tutor doubles as a research instrument. Current questions concern how students actually use a conversational tutor, what usage volume reveals about study behaviour, whether the tool changes measured learning outcomes, and where its limitations show — including variation in how much learners trust generative output. Findings inform the AI literacy curriculum described on the AI Education page.
